Detection

Sentinel-2 supplies the spectral evidence and Sentinel-1 the structural evidence. Only where the two agree is a patch called clearing; a detection on one sensor alone is reported, not discarded, because the single-sensor tiers are informative in themselves.

Confirmed (S1 + S2) — Both sensors agree: the canopy went and the structure went with it.Sentinel-2 only — Spectral loss with no matching structural loss.Sentinel-1 only — Structural loss with no matching spectral loss.

Regrowth

Each confirmed patch is dated from its own time series, then followed on three tracks: NDVI for greenness, NBR for canopy condition, and Sentinel-1 VH for structure. They are deliberately reported side by side. Grass colonises a cleared paddock within a season and pushes NDVI back towards baseline while no woody vegetation has returned at all, so a patch whose NDVI has recovered but whose NBR and VH have not is grassland, not regrowth.

Recovered — Back to at least 80% of the pre-clearing baseline (R80P).Recovering — Trending up but not yet at 80% of baseline.Stalled — Well below baseline with no meaningful upward trend - the site is being held open, by grazing, repeat cultivation or drought.Recleared — Recovered part-way, then dropped again: a second clearing or disturbance event on the same ground.

Where the three tracks disagree

Observed recovery fraction at fixed ages, averaged across patches. NDVI sits consistently above NBR: greenness returns faster than canopy condition does, because ground cover colonises the site long before woody vegetation does. VH sits above both, for a different reason - C-band backscatter responds steeply to the first increments of woody structure and then saturates, which makes it a sensitive early-regrowth indicator and a weak one for separating mature regrowth. No single track is the answer; the disagreement between them is the information.

Validation

Assessed against the reference truth that ships with the synthetic datacube. A single overall accuracy would be meaningless here - change is rare, so a map detecting nothing would score above 99%. What follows is recall by patch size, precision against the specific things that mimic clearing, and total area bias.

Recall by patch size

Where the map stops working. The smallest class sits below the 0.5 ha minimum mapping unit and is removed by the sieve by design, not missed by the detector.

What the look-alikes did

This is the argument for fusing two sensors, in one table. A burn scar and a fallowed paddock both read as clearing to Sentinel-2 alone; neither survives the requirement that Sentinel-1 agree.

How soon could each sensor have said so?

Days between the clearing event and the first acquisition on which that sensor could have raised the alert. Sentinel-2 has to wait for a view of the ground; over inland NSW in summer, under cloud and bushfire smoke, that wait is what sets the response time of the whole program.

Sentinel-1 (radar)Sentinel-2 (optical)
Median latency: Sentinel-1 2 days (worst 5), Sentinel-2 16 days (worst 51).
